three differences: (1) pandas reads role hw-reset-request-sum, the SQL contract and NF role is hot-water-reset-request-sum, so the harness gives pandas no input and it skips; (2) SQL faults at request sum <= request_lo, pandas at < request_lo; (3) pandas applies the hydronic-flow gate with a 600 s startup holdoff. Follow-up: align names and comparison with the owner (see #1582)

pandas operational gate holds a fan-running rule for startup_delay_seconds=600 after the fan proves on, SQL has no startup holdoff: a fault already present at fan start is confirmed one 5-minute sample earlier in SQL per fan start (0.1667 h over the two fan starts of the 8-equipment 7-day run); with the gate off pandas equals SQL

Series starts with the fan already running (edge DST-week start is 18:00 local): pandas applies its 600 s operational startup holdoff at the first sample, SQL has none, so SQL confirms one 5-minute sample earlier. Verified: trimming the first 6 h of rows makes SQL equal pandas.
Same cause as FC8: the series begins with the fan already running; pandas holds off 600 s from the first sample, SQL does not (verified by trimming the start).

Two input-handling differences: (1) NULL zone_t cells: SQL drops NULL rows (WHERE zone_t IS NOT NULL) and holds the previous sample's state across the null run, pandas scores a NULL as not faulted; (2) planted out-of-range zone_t (80 degC): the pandas quality layer marks it OUT_OF_RANGE and excludes it, SQL scores the value as given.
Planted out-of-range zone_t (80 degC): the pandas quality layer marks those samples OUT_OF_RANGE and excludes them, SQL computes zone_t - sat on the value as given and faults.

Duplicate (equipment, timestamp) rows: SQL scores the rows as delivered, the reference de-duplicates first (the input contract is one row per timestamp). Verified: de-duplicating the rows before SQL makes SQL equal pandas.

Gap handling: SQL flags |oa_t - previous sample| above the fixed limit whatever the time between samples, pandas scales the limit by the sample gap (limit x dt/poll), so a real change across a >2 h gap is a spike in SQL only.
